Weekend Car Scheme

Government initiative introduced on 1 May 1991 to enable more people to own cars without contributing to traffic congestion. Under this scheme, car owners would only be allowed to drive between the hours of 7pm to 7am on weekdays, after 3pm on Saturday and all day on Sunday and public holidays. They were also given a full rebate of the net Additional Registration Fee (ARF), import duty and Certificate of Entitlement (COE) up to a maximum of $15,000. The scheme was revamped in 1994 and became known as the Off-Peak Car (OPC) scheme.
